item.title: Enugu APC urges residents to verify political claims
item.description: By Dennis Agbo The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Enugu State has urged residents to exercise caution when receiving and sharing political information ahead of the 2027 general elections. The APC Campaign Council’s Spokesperson and Director of Public Communications, Steve Oruruo, made the appeal in a statement titled, “Unmasking the Alarmism of NDC: A Clarion Call for Enugu’s Extra Vigilance.” Oruruo referred to public discussions surrounding the management of Amadeo Event Centre and a proposed town hall meeting involving the New Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi. He said the disagreement over the use of the facility was a matter involving the parties to a private agreement and urged political stakeholders to avoid drawing conclusions about the involvement of the state government without verified information. The APC spokesperson also called on residents to verify reports, particularly those circulating on social media, before accepting or sharing them. He said political discussions ahead of the 2027 elections should focus on candidates’ ideas, policies and capacity to deliver good governance. Oruruo further highlighted the development programmes of Governor Peter Mbah’s administration, expressing confidence that the government’s record would feature prominently in the electoral contest. He urged Ndi Enugu to remain vigilant, promote issue-based political engagement and assess the proposals and records of political parties as the state approaches the 2027 general elections. item.title: ‘I searched and found’ – Pastor Jimmy Odukoya confirms marriage to Pastor Mo Jasmine
item.description: Former Nollywood actor turned cleric, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has confirmed his marriage to his fiancée, Pastor Mo Jasmine. Odukoya made the announcement during a church service, where he invited his new wife onto the altar and introduced her to the congregation. The confirmation comes a day after the cleric hinted that he had found love again, sharing a photograph of his and his fiancée’s hands, both wearing rings. Sharing their love story with the congregation, Odukoya said he had been searching for a suitable partner before finding his wife. “You know, the Bible said it is not good, it said I will find someone suitable. When Adam saw, he said this is the flesh of my flesh, bone of my bone, I was looking and searching, and I found. Some of you saw the post, some people said is it artwork, no it’s my wife; allow me to introduce to you for the first time, Pastor Mrs. Odukoya, a new first lady, my wife. Pastor Mo Odukoya,” he said. The marriage marks a new chapter in Odukoya’s personal life following the end of his previous marriage to Oluwakemi Sade Banjoko. The former couple got married in London in March 2013 and had two children together before their separation. item.title: Adeleke, Oyetola unite to deliver 1.5m votes for Tinubu
item.description: Tompolo donates 30 campaign vehicles, launches 10,000 canvassers By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The re-election campaign of President Bola Tinubu in Osun State received a boost at the weekend as Governor Ademola Adeleke and his predecessor, Adegboyega Oyetola, pledged to work together to secure victory for the President in the 2027 election. The commitment came as the Grand Patron of the President Bola Tinubu Door-to-Door Movement, High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, launched 10,000 canvassers and donated 30 campaign vehicles and public address systems to support the mobilisation drive. Speaking at the launch held at Freedom Park, Osogbo, representatives of Adeleke and Oyetola called on political leaders and stakeholders to set aside their differences and work towards delivering the targeted 1.5 million votes for Tinubu in the state. Oyetola, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, who was represented by Bola Oyebamiji, urged the canvassers to approach the assignment with sincerity, discipline and commitment. He cautioned them against hypocrisy, political pretence and complacency, while appealing to political leaders, interest groups and other stakeholders to put aside personal interests and differences. “I appeal to all political leaders, interest groups, individuals and stakeholders to rise above selfish interests, personal ego and political differences. Let us demonstrate that political differences need not prevent us from pursuing a shared national objective. “With unity of purpose, effective grassroots mobilisation and unwavering commitment, we can deliver the 1.5 million votes targeted for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Osun State and secure victory for our party’s candidates at all levels,” he said. In his remarks, Adeleke, who is the state coordinator of the Presidential Campaign Council and was represented by his deputy, Kola Adewusi, described the launch of the canvassers and donation of vehicles as timely for the commencement of the President’s campaign in the state. He urged coalition partners to put aside past disagreements and work together, saying the partnership was focused primarily on the presidential election. “Our gathering is therefore a timely push to gain further momentum in the campaign process. We must therefore forget past disagreements and unite to deliver for the President. “All coalition partners have a duty to overlook all previous relationship antagonism and join hands to deliver between 1.5 to 2 million votes for Mr President,” he said. Earlier, Tompolo, who was represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, Dr Kestin Pondi, said the movement was targeting at least 90 per cent of the votes in Osun for Tinubu. “We know that you are already going to vote for your brother. item.title: Osun group demands arrest of Sowore’s attackers
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo A coalition of civil society organisations in Osun State, The Osun Masterminds (TOM), has condemned the reported attack on the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Mr Omoyele Sowore, in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State, and called on security agencies to identify and prosecute those responsible. The group described the incident as a national disgrace and an assault on Nigerians’ rights to participate in politics, express their views and support candidates of their choice. TOM’s Executive Director, Professor Wasiu Oyedokun-Alli, made the position known during the group’s monthly briefing on the state of the nation. He said elections should provide an opportunity for candidates and political parties to present their policies and development plans to the electorate, rather than become occasions for violence and intimidation. “Elections should be a festival of ideas, a peaceful contest of developmental blueprints, and a developmental milestone where the sovereign will of the people is freely expressed,” he said. Oyedokun-Alli called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant agencies to investigate the reported attack and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. “We call on the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services (DSS), and all relevant statutory agencies to rise above partisan politics and uphold the rule of law,” he said. The group expressed concern that the political environment was becoming increasingly hostile to opposition figures and Nigerians expressing dissenting views. It alleged that the electoral space was being turned into a combat zone where opposition figures and dissenting voices were targeted, silenced and physically assaulted. Describing the reported attack as a national disgrace, particularly because it allegedly occurred in a public space, TOM also criticised what it said were attempts by security agencies and law enforcement authorities to downplay attacks on political figures. “When security apparatuses and law enforcement agencies trivialize such high-profile acts of violence—dismissing life-threatening injuries as ‘minor’ or engaging in administrative denials—they surrender their neutrality and embolden the forces of tyranny,” the group stated. Oyedokun-Alli warned that Nigeria could not guarantee credible, free and fair elections in 2027 if political violence was allowed to prevent candidates from campaigning and engaging with voters. item.title: Lagos begins joint enforcement of badges for Danfo operators
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The Lagos State Government has announced plans to commence joint enforcement of compulsory identification badges and other regulatory requirements for commercial bus operators, popularly known as Danfo drivers and conductors, to strengthen commuter safety and accountability. The enforcement drive, being coordinated by the State Ministry of Transportation through its Directorate of Public Transport and Commuter Services (PTCS), will involve the Vehicle Inspection Service (VIS) and the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA). The Director of Public Transport and Commuter Services, Mr Nuhman Edu, said the initiative was designed to improve commuter security, ensure accountability among transport operators and strengthen compliance with established transport regulations. He identified some of the major compliance gaps the exercise would address to include improper commuter vehicle registration, absence of vehicle body tags, stage carriage permits, drivers’ badges and conductors’ badges. Edu explained that the collaboration with VIS and LASTMA would strengthen the verification of relevant safety documents during routine enforcement operations. “Where a vehicle is found to be non-compliant, enforcement or compliance procedures will be initiated strictly in accordance with extant laws, regulations, approved guidelines and established operational procedures,” he said. He said proper identification of commercial vehicles, drivers and conductors would make operators traceable, improve accountability, assist investigations involving vehicles allegedly used in criminal activities and facilitate the prompt resolution of commuter complaints. According to him, the framework will clearly define the responsibilities of the participating agencies across six areas. These include verification of prescribed PTCS documents, recording of vehicle compliance status, identification of violations, initiation of enforcement or corrective measures, information exchange and data-sharing, as well as referral of cases requiring further administrative or regulatory action. Edu said commuter safety and security remained the primary reasons for strengthening regulation of public transportation in the state. He added that the ministry would engage transport unions and associations through stakeholder meetings, media campaigns and sensitisation programmes to ensure operators understood the requirements. The director further disclosed that the ministry had resolved to introduce continuous monitoring, evaluation and assessment of compliance levels across the state, supported by reporting and feedback mechanisms to ensure timely identification and resolution of regulatory gaps. item.title: ‘It was a prayer walk’ – Pastor Adeboye denies carrying placard against Jonathan
item.description: The General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG), Pastor Enoch Adeboye, has faulted media reports regarding a placard he carried during a prayer walk under former President Goodluck Jonathan’s administration. The cleric spoke on Sunday during the church’s November Thanksgiving service, where he accused a journalist of misrepresenting the incident and portraying him as a wicked person for allegedly carrying a placard against the former president. Recounting how he came across the report, Adeboye said he was initially amused by the claim. “Recently, somebody wrote in the papers, or said somehow, ‘Pastor Adeboye is a very wicked man. After all, we know that not too long ago, he carried a placard against President Goodluck Jonathan,’” he said. While admitting that he carried a placard, the cleric insisted that the exercise was a prayer walk and not a protest against Jonathan. “True, I carried a placard. I can’t deny that. It was important. It was a prayer walk. We wanted to pray,” he said. He explained that the exercise followed a directive asking churches to organise prayer walks around their premises. “The chairman said all churches should do a prayer walk near their churches. That’s what I did,” he said. Adeboye further argued that the date of the exercise contradicted the report’s suggestion that he carried the placard against Jonathan while he was president. “But I carried the placard in 2020. Jonathan ceased to be president in 2015. I carried the placard five years in the second term of Buhari,” Adeboye said. He accused the journalist of distorting the facts and criticised the failure to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident before publishing the report. “But a journalist twisted it. I said, I did what I did in 2015. And everybody swallowed it,” he said. The RCCG leader also recalled his exposure to journalism studies in the 1960s, saying he was taught the importance of investigative journalism and verifying information before publication. “I remember in those days in the Department of Journalism, when you go there and you take a course, they talked about something called investigative journalism,” he said. He added, “That things don’t appear as they may seem. Investigate, if you have a story, before you take it to the press.” Vanguard News The post ‘It was a prayer walk’ – Pastor Adeboye denies carrying placard against Jonathan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Vanguard, TVC, Channels, others fix November 8 for Lagos governorship debate
item.description: LAGOS — The Nigeria Debate Consortium has fixed November 8, 2026, for a governorship debate involving candidates contesting the 2027 Lagos State governorship election. The debate, scheduled for 7 p.m., will hold at The Hub by IALA, House of His Glory, Plot 18, Providence Road, beside Keystone Bank, Marwa, Lekki, Lagos. The consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, TheCable and Vanguard Newspaper, said the debate would kick-start its series of electoral engagements ahead of the 2027 general elections, covering selected battleground states before culminating in a presidential debate and town hall. In a statement announcing the event, the consortium said the initiative was designed to provide a credible, non-partisan platform for governorship candidates to present their agendas, defend their policy choices and respond to questions on issues affecting Lagos residents. It said the debate would focus on critical areas, including transportation, infrastructure, security, housing, education, healthcare, job creation and economic growth, allowing voters to assess the candidates’ proposals and readiness to govern. Channels Television said the initiative reflected the media’s responsibility to inform the electorate and strengthen democratic accountability. “Voters deserve more than campaign promises; they deserve clear answers, credible plans and an opportunity to assess those seeking their mandate,” the organisation said. It added that the debate would place issues, ideas and the future of Lagos at the centre of the electoral conversation, helping citizens make informed choices based on candidates’ proposals and their capacity to deliver. Similarly, TVC News described the debate as an opportunity for candidates to move beyond political rhetoric and demonstrate the substance of their vision for the state. “Citizens need to understand not only what candidates promise, but how they intend to deliver,” it said, adding that a fair platform for such engagement would promote accountability and an informed electorate. The consortium said the debate would be conducted in line with established professional standards, with fairness, neutrality, equal opportunity and editorial independence as guiding principles. It added that all participating candidates would be subjected to the same rules, speaking times and moderation standards. Experienced journalists are expected to moderate the debate, which will be broadcast to national and digital audiences through the participating media organisations’ platforms. The consortium called on Lagos residents, particularly eligible voters, young people, civil society organisations, professional groups and the business community, to follow the debate and engage with the issues and choices facing the state. The statement was jointly signed by Babajide Kolade-Otitoju, Director of News, TVC News, and Kingsley Uranta, General Manager, Channels Television. item.title: Germany ‘Gen Z Regelt’ Protest Turned Violent As Rioters Loot Shops
item.description: Masked rioters looted shops in the German city of Frankfurt on Saturday as massive demonstrations turned violent across the country, with police also firing water cannons at youths hurling Molotov cocktails. Several police officers were injured in the violence after tens of thousands joined youth-led protests across the country organised by the group “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!). The demonstrations, inspired by similar movements in France and Italy calling for political elites to heed the concerns of the younger generation, were largely peaceful during the day. But tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of young people refused to disperse, with violence breaking out in major cities including Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg. It was especially bad in the financial hub of Frankfurt, where police faced protesters hurling stones, fireworks and petrol bombs, and responded with water cannon and pepper spray. “Violent riots” were taking place, police said in a statement. “Windows have been smashed at several shops. Molotov cocktails are also being thrown at emergency personnel.” Protesters light flares after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” (Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP) A gun store was among the shops looted, with its windows smashed. Police said they arrested a suspect and seized two weapons. A trainer shop and a perfume store were also targeted, the Bild daily reported. A large section of Frankfurt’s main shopping street was closed off as authorities sought to quell the unrest, with police vans and riot police stopping anyone from entering, according to an AFP journalist. A police helicopter hovered overhead as sporadic blasts were heard on the street. At least one police officer was injured there and was receiving medical treatment. ‘Shameful’ Roman Poseck, interior minister of Hesse state, said that “around 100 clearly identified left-wing extremists” had infiltrated the protest in Frankfurt. “It is shameful how this event here in Frankfurt has ended.” Police also used water cannon in the cities of Hamburg and Cologne after they said demonstrators targeted emergency service workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. Riot Police block the street in front of protesters after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” (Photo by KIRILL KUDRYAVTSEV / AFP) In Berlin, a protest not organised by the “GenZ regelt!” movement took place in the evening, with police reporting they were pelted with eggs and bottles. A police officer in Bonn suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group. Police were reported to have arrested large numbers of rioters. The youth-led protests earlier in the day took place in a mostly peaceful and festive atmosphere. Some people were dressed in outfits ranging from dinosaurs to Batman as the demonstrations coincided with Halloween. item.title: Army rescues 11 kidnapped victims in Kebbi operations
item.description: Troops of Sector 2, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, have rescued 11 kidnapped victims in Danko-Wasagu Local Government Area of Kebbi in two separate encounters. The operations, deployed for counter-terrorism and anti-banditry, took place on Oct. 30 and 31. The Acting Deputy Director of Army Public Relations for 8 Division, Nigerian Army, Lt-Col. Osoba Olaniyi, confirmed this in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria in Birnin Kebbi on Sunday. He revealed that: “in the first operation, the troops responded to a distress call reporting that armed bandits have blocked a road leading to Ribah town and attempted to enter the town. “On arrival, troops found that an unspecified number of civilians have been kidnapped and some motorcycles were abandoned at the scene. “Troops immediately pursued the bandits and exchanged fire with them, forcing them to abandon seven kidnapped victims.” Olaniyi listed the rescued victims as Sa’adu Bala, Dantani Yahyi, Nura Musa, Nasiru Muhammad, Abdulakeem Abubakar, Abdulahi Maikudi and Zaki Gom. The acting director said the rescued persons had been reunited with their families. Speaking on the second operation, Olaniyi said the troops were on patrol in the Wasagu area when they came under fire from terrorists. “The troops responded decisively, forcing the terrorists to flee and abandon four victims who had earlier been abducted from their farms in Wasagu village. “The rescued victims were Lawali Ali, Samaila Shuaibu, Kasimu Shuaibu and Aliyu Bala, all of Wasagu village. They were handed over to the community head,” he said. Olaniyi reiterated the determination of the troops to the safety and security of all communities in the area, assuring that they would continue to respond promptly to security threats. item.title: Photos: Sanwo-Olu walks runway alongside models at Lagos Fashion Week
item.description: Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has made a surprise appearance on the runway at the 2026 Lagos Fashion Week, joining models to showcase a fashion ensemble. The governor was dressed by Nigerian designer Ugo Monye in regal off-white attire that blended the traditional caftan with a kimono-inspired design. He completed the look with a beige fedora. Sanwo-Olu walked confidently across the runway, drawing applause from the audience as he flashed peace signs and exchanged nods with spectators. I stepped away from the usual business of governance to walk the runway for the incredibly talented Ugo Monye at Lagos Fashion Week. Lagos continues to grow as a home for fashion, creativity and culture and I am always happy to support the people driving this growth. pic.twitter.com/B1tnMiiSoh — Babajide Sanwo-Olu (@jidesanwoolu) October 31, 2026 The 2026 Lagos Fashion Week, themed “CRAFTED: Heritage”, began last Wednesday at the Federal Palace Hotel in Lagos and is scheduled to end on Sunday. The annual fashion event brings together designers, models, industry professionals and fashion enthusiasts to celebrate African creativity, craftsmanship and heritage. item.title: Obi accuses Tinubu of neglecting Imo, cites insecurity, poverty
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has accused President Bola Tinubu of neglecting Imo State, alleging that the President has not spent a night in the state since assuming office despite spending more than 260 days abroad. Obi made the allegation during a town hall meeting in Owerri, Imo State, on Saturday, October 31, 2026, as part of his ongoing nationwide engagement with Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement posted on his X handle on Sunday, Obi said he had earlier visited a market in Owerri, where he interacted with traders, buyers and other residents about their economic challenges. He said their accounts reflected the difficulties ordinary Nigerians were facing under the economic policies of the Tinubu administration. At the town hall meeting, the former Anambra State governor criticised the Federal Government over what he described as rising national debt without corresponding improvements in citizens’ living conditions. He also raised concerns about poverty, hunger, insecurity and out-of-school children, claiming that more than 140 million Nigerians were living in multidimensional poverty, while approximately 18 million children were out of school. Obi further described Nigeria as one of the world’s most terrorised countries, arguing that the country was facing multiple economic and security challenges. Reassuring residents that the country could overcome its challenges, the NDC candidate said he and his running mate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, were committed to securing and uniting the country. He also pledged massive investments in critical sectors, particularly healthcare and education, as well as policies aimed at lifting millions of Nigerians out of poverty. Obi said the duo possessed the experience, competence, capacity and commitment required to address the country’s challenges. During the interactive session, he said participants also raised questions about the protection of their votes in the 2027 elections. He urged voters to turn out in large numbers, exercise their democratic rights and remain at their polling units until the final results were declared. Obi expressed appreciation to his supporters, party candidates, members and organisers, as well as residents of Imo State, for their reception and support. He described the task of building a new Nigeria as a collective responsibility, expressing optimism that the country could work for all its citizens. item.title: 2027: South-East ready to return Tinubu, Shettima, Kalu claims
item.description: The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Okezie Kalu, has claimed that the South-East has resolved to support the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima in 2027. Kalu said the region was prepared to return the APC-led administration for another term in appreciation of what he described as Tinubu’s support for the Igbo people. He spoke on Saturday at the flag-off of the APC Women’s Mobilisation Campaign and South-East Women Empowerment Programme, organised by the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, in Enugu. The Deputy Speaker, who is also the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council 11 (South), said the immediate political responsibility of the Igbo people was to support a leader who, according to him, had demonstrated commitment to their interests. He recalled that Tinubu, during his tenure as governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007, appointed Igbo people into his administration. “This man has not hidden his love for Ndi Igbo. During his time as the governor of Lagos State, no Igbo property was taken. Nobody who was a businessman in Lagos was arrested. Mr Ben Akabueze was an Igbo man that he brought into his cabinet as governor. It has never happened before. I hope we will reciprocate his kind gestures to Ndi Igbo. We must do so this time,” he said. Kalu also recalled the post-civil war promise of Reconstruction, Rehabilitation and Reintegration (3Rs), arguing that successive administrations had failed to fulfil the commitment to the people of the South-East until Tinubu assumed office. He cited the signing into law of the South-East Development Commission Bill as evidence of the President’s commitment to the region. “I also need to remind you that after the civil war, we waited for almost 60 years for a promise that was made to the people of Igbo land that was not kept. The 3Rs: Reconciliation, Reconstruction and Reintegration. Was the promise kept or not? It wasn’t kept. “Government after government but they ignored us. Administration after administration, they ignored the Igbo and we were waiting and asking, when will the messiah come to save the Igbo? Then came a man who loves the Igbo from his heart,” he said. The Deputy Speaker added that the South-East Development Commission Bill had remained pending through successive assemblies before Tinubu signed it into law. “South-East Development Commission Bill has been in the Parliament from year to year, Assembly to Assembly, they refused to sign it into law. But when President Tinubu came, South-East Development Commission became a commission under the law. Tinubu is a warrior, a great President,” he added. Kalu further listed road construction, bridge projects, scholarships and loans among the interventions he said the Federal Government had undertaken in the region, while commending the First Lady for her women’s empowerment initiatives. item.title: INEC: Attacks on corps members, election officials will attract full legal consequences
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Professor Joash O. Amupitan, SAN, has warned that anyone who attacks or threatens National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and other election officials during the 2027 general elections will face the full weight of the law. Amupitan gave the warning on Saturday, October 31, 2026, at the South-South Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. INEC disclosed this in a statement posted on its X handle on Sunday. The INEC chairman also charged electoral officials across the South-South geopolitical zone to uphold impartiality, discipline and accountability as the commission intensifies preparations for the 2027 general elections. He warned that partisanship, negligence, absenteeism and financial impropriety would attract disciplinary action. Amupitan said the assessment was part of the commission’s field-based approach to evaluating operational preparedness, identifying gaps and strengthening service delivery ahead of the elections. He cited INEC’s conduct of governorship elections in Anambra, Ekiti and Osun states, FCT Area Council elections and 16 by-elections as experiences informing preparations for the nationwide exercise. He disclosed that the South-South zone had 15,823,550 registered voters, including 3,736,434 in Rivers State, stressing that no eligible voter should be disenfranchised through administrative negligence or logistical failure. On electoral technology, Amupitan said the commission was preparing its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), including 57,000 newly procured devices, while auditing electronic result management systems to strengthen transparency in result transmission through the INEC Result Viewing (IReV) portal. Addressing concerns over suspicious photographs on the preliminary voters’ register published online, he said the commission was examining the records and would take corrective action based on verified findings. He urged members of the public to participate in the display, claims and objections process ahead of the publication of the final register scheduled for December 15, 2026. The chairman also highlighted the logistical challenges posed by the region’s creeks, coastal settlements and riverine communities. He disclosed that INEC had finalised a Memorandum of Understanding with the Maritime Transporters Union to support the timely and secure transportation of election personnel and materials. On election security, Amupitan reaffirmed the commission’s collaboration with security agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), emphasising intelligence-led planning and the protection of voters, electoral materials and personnel. He warned that anyone who threatens or harms INEC officials, including NYSC members deployed for election duties, would face the full weight of the law. item.title: EPL: ‘We can beat Arsenal’ – Liverpool coach Iraola speaks ahead of Sunday clash
item.description: Andoni Iraola is pleased his side’s performances have left some Liverpool fans dreaming of a Premier League title challenge ahead of Sunday’s match at home to champions Arsenal, even if it is too soon for him to pay much attention to the table. Victory at Anfield would see Liverpool move to within three points of Arsenal, who are currently level at the top of the table with leaders Manchester City. Liverpool are on a five-game winning run in all competitions, a sure sign of their progress as they adapt to the methods of former Bournemouth manager Iraola in his first season on Merseyside since replacing the sacked Arne Slot. But Iraola said Friday: “It is still October. We have to take one game at a time and I always say the reference is more or less when we’ve played against each other once so halfway through the season. That’s when you can start to look at the standings. “Right now, we are in a position where we need to improve and keep getting better.” But asked if he welcomed the increasingly buoyant mood among Liverpool fans, the Spaniard replied: “For fans, it is good if they have expectations or they think we can win.” Arsenal moved level with City at the top of the table following a 2-0 win over Everton last weekend, but then suffered a huge upset defeat on Tuesday after being knocked out of the League Cup on penalties by fourth-tier Fleetwood. “We know Arsenal and how good they are,” Iraola said. “They have very good players, working a lot in synchronicity and we have to be ready for that challenge. “It’s going to be a demanding game but we also trust our players, trust ourselves and in the good atmosphere we will for sure have on Sunday. I hope we will be at a level to win this game.” As for Liverpool’s recent run, a cautious Iraola said: “It is five wins (in a row) but just two are in the league so if we are talking about the league we still need more wins to recover points. “But definitely we know what we want in terms of we have to improve a lot of things. But, if you can do this process while you are getting results, it is always nice.” Vanguard News The post EPL: ‘We can beat Arsenal’ – Liverpool coach Iraola speaks ahead of Sunday clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gunmen attack Plateau military checkpoint, kill soldier, steal weapons
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Gunmen have attacked troops of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP) at a checkpoint in Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State, killing a soldier and carting away two weapons. The attack occurred at about 8pm on Saturday at Sopp Checkpoint in Ungwan Boka, Riyom LGA. Our correspondent gathered that the troops were keeping vigil at the checkpoint when the attackers opened fire on them from different directions, triggering a gun battle. Security sources said the gunmen fled into the surrounding bushes after the exchange of fire. Confirming the incident, the spokesman of OPEP, Captain Chinonso Polycarp Oteh, described the attack as deliberate and unprovoked, adding that troops had restored normalcy in the area. Oteh said, “It was a deliberate and unprovoked attack on troops at Sopp Checkpoint, Ungwan Boka in Riyom Local Government Area. “Troops have restored normalcy in the area and are maintaining aggressive pursuit of the perpetrators in order to apprehend them and recover the carted-away weapons.” He said the situation remained under control, while troops continued to maintain heightened vigilance to prevent further security breaches and reassure residents of their safety. The spokesman urged members of the public to remain calm, go about their lawful activities and provide credible information that could assist security agencies in their ongoing operations. item.title: Kane Misses Penalty After Ballon d’Or Feat As Bayern Held By Dortmund
item.description: Fabio Silva’s 89th-minute goal earned Borussia Dortmund a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich after Harry Kane missed a penalty in a see-saw Bundesliga clash on Saturday. Bayern were 1-0 up when Kane, playing his first match since winning the Ballon d’Or on Monday, rattled his second-half spot kick against the crossbar. Dortmund’s Serhou Guirassy levelled shortly after, but Kane helped Bayern retake the lead when he set up a Dayot Upamecano goal. In the final minute, substitutes Konstantinos Karetsas and Silva combined to grab Dortmund a share of the spoils. “Coming back twice here in Munich is no easy feat. We earned a well-deserved point here today,” Dortmund coach Niko Kovac told Sky Germany, adding his side “never stopped believing in ourselves.” Dortmund’s Guinean forward #09 Serhou Guirassy (C) scores the 1-1 goal during the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) The result leaves the two sides level atop the Bundesliga table, with defending champions Bayern ahead on goal difference. It is just the fourth time in the past 18 ‘Klassiker’ matches that Bayern have not emerged victorious. In addition to the late draw, Bayern, who are without Vincent Kompany as he recovers from a virus, will be concerned by further injuries to their undermanned forward line ahead of Tuesday’s trip to Atletico Madrid. Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise were all subbed out on Saturday, with Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz already out with injury. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said the draw appeared “costly”, with Saibari and Gnabry’s injuries “somewhat serious”. Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich, who returned after missing three matches after the sudden death of his father, said: “It’s been a really, really hard week, but you can forget during the game. “Other than the result today, you have to say we’re going through difficult moments right now, now with the injuries we picked up.” Kane was honoured pre-match with his Ballon d’Or shown to the Bayern faithful for the first time. Bayern Munich’s English forward Harry Kane shows his Ballon d’Or trophy to the fans prior to the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and BVB Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on October 31, 2026. item.title: Clashes Erupt In France As Thousands Protest Cost Of Living, Inequality
item.description: A police officer in Paris was injured after being struck by a Molotov cocktail as clashes erupted in the capital and other cities during protests across France against soaring living costs and inequality. Hundreds of thousands of people, some dressed for Halloween, demonstrated across France in a third consecutive weekend of largely peaceful demonstrations. But the Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez pointed to an “extraordinary” level of violence from some, blaming far-left extremist groups for attacks on security forces. He described the throwing of a Molotov cocktail at a riot police officer in Paris as an “attempted murder,” adding that the officer had escaped with minor injuries. “We are fully prepared for those looking for confrontation tonight,” he added. After a march on the outskirts of Paris in bright sunshine, clashes broke out between police and some demonstrators as the procession reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to pry up paving stones and hurl them at police, AFP journalists saw. Police responded with tear gas and several baton charges. ‘Engulfed In Flames’ Far-right leader Marine Le Pen said those responsible for the Molotov attack must be “punished with the utmost severity.” “The images of a police officer engulfed in flames after being targeted with incendiary devices are unbearable,” Le Pen said on X. A French riot gendarme mobile has flames rising up his uniform after being hit by a Molotov cocktail during a charge against demonstrators at the end of a demonstration part of a nationwide day of protests over the rising cost of living and inequality organised by Yellow Vest movement, labour unions and high school and university students organisations, in Paris on October 31, 2026. Photo by SAMEER AL-DOUMY / AFP A night-time curfew was to be imposed in the central Paris Republique and Chatelet-Les Halles neighbourhoods from 11:00 pm to 6:00 am on Saturday and Sunday. Police arrested more than 420 people across the country. The interior ministry said that “radical elements” in cities including Bordeaux, Toulouse and Marseille had attempted to enter city centres “with the aim of carrying out vandalism and looting”. In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas. In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorised protest that drew several thousand people. ‘Attack On Freedom’ Earlier Saturday, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, marched through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. item.title: German Police, Protesters Clash After ‘Gen Z’ Protest, Several Police Officers Injured
item.description: German police and protesters clashed across the country Saturday following massive youth-led protests, with authorities using water cannon and pepper spray as masked demonstrators hurled fireworks, stones and bottles. Several police officers were injured in the violence after tens of thousands joined protests nationwide that were organised by the group “GenZ regelt!” (Gen Z has got this!). The demonstrations, inspired by similar movements in France and Italy calling for political elites to heed the concerns of the younger generation, were largely peaceful during the day. But tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of protesters refused to disperse. Police were pelted with projectiles in the western city of Frankfurt, and responded by using water cannon and pepper spray as they sought to clear protesters. “Incidents of stones and fireworks being thrown at the emergency services continue to occur,” police said on X. “We are taking action against these troublemakers.” Police also used water cannon in the cities of Hamburg and Cologne after they said demonstrators targeted emergency service workers with fireworks, stones and bottles. ‘Boiling Point’ In Berlin, a protest that was not organised by the “GenZ regelt!” movement took place in the evening, with police reporting they were pelted with eggs and bottles. Police in the eastern city of Leipzig also used pepper spray after protests turned violent while a police officer in Bonn suffered minor injuries during a confrontation with a group. Police were reported to have made several arrests. Police detain a protester after a demonstration organised by “GenZ regelt!” Photo by RALF HIRSCHBERGER / AFP The youth-led protests earlier in the day took place in a mostly peaceful and festive atmosphere, with some dressed in outfits ranging from dinosaurs to Batman as the demonstrations coincided with Halloween.They waved signs that read “Time for resistance”, and “Merz must go”, in reference to conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz. “I think it’s really important to show solidarity with all the other protests currently happening across Europe, including in France,” Milla, a 20-year-old student who only gave her first name, told AFP in Berlin. “I’ve been waiting for a long time for something to finally really happen, and for people to tackle this with a bit more force. I believe that today here is the first step.” Marius, a 23-year-old care worker, added that “politicians need to know about this… the situation is slowly reaching boiling point.” “I think we can all feel that this just isn’t working anymore,” he added. The movement’s complaints range from the high cost of living to poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts and, more broadly, what it sees as politicians making decisions with apparently little regard for the younger generation. item.title: Katsina Debunks Campaign Violence Claims, Orders Probe Into Yankara Incident
item.description: The Katsina State Government has dismissed reports linking the incident that occurred in Yankara, Faskari Local Government Area, to Governor Dikko Radda’s Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign, describing such claims as false and misleading. In a statement, the government said preliminary findings showed that the disturbance stemmed from a disagreement between participants in a Maulud procession and security personnel over designated procession routes, resulting in confusion along a public street in Yankara. It stressed that the incident was entirely unrelated to thegovernor’s campaign activities or the Tinubu-Dikko campaign rally held in Faskari. According to the government, Governor Radda passed through Yankara without incident on his way to Faskari, where he paid a courtesy visit to the District Head’s Palace and was received by the district head and other traditional rulers. The governor, it said, later proceeded to the Faskari Local Government secretariat, where he inspected ongoing renovation works at the secretariat and council chambers before attending the campaign rally and interacting with residents and supporters. Governor Dikko Radda addresses a crowd of supporters at the Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign in Faskari Local Government Area of Katsina State on October 31, 2026. The state government urged relevant security agencies to carry out a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that those responsible are identified where necessary. In the statement signed by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Ibrahim Mohammed, the government appealed to residents to remain calm, uphold peace, and avoid spreading unverified information capable of causing unnecessary tension. Violence was reported in Yankara town on Saturday after suspected hoodlums attacked supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC), leaving several people injured and a campaign vehicle set ablaze. Eyewitnesses said the attackers allegedly ambushed APC supporters heading to Governor Radda’s campaign rally in Faskari, disrupting movement along the major road and causing panic among residents. Angry youths were also alleged to have blocked the route the campaign convoy was expected to use.
